name: Cannabis / CBD for sleep

card.summary: Cannabis and cannabidiol are used for sleep onset, but clinical evidence is limited and CBD supplements are not FDA-approved for sleep.
card.note: CBD products are often mislabeled; FDA has raised liver, drug-interaction and fertility concerns.

quick.overview:
Some people use cannabis products or cannabidiol (CBD) to fall asleep. Wikipedia's CBD article says clinical evidence for sleep benefit is limited, and lists sleepiness as a common effect and insomnia among adverse effects of the approved drug Epidiolex.
Only small trials have been registered, for example a phase 2 study of cannabinoids for insomnia in major depression with 14 participants.
quick.mechanism: CBD is a non-intoxicating cannabis constituent whose sleep-related mechanisms remain unestablished. THC is the main intoxicating compound.
quick.risks: The FDA has cited possible liver toxicity, drug interactions, effects on mood and alertness, and unknown long-term effects. FDA studies found many CBD products were inaccurately labeled and about half of 147 tested contained THC. Legal status varies widely.

lead: Cannabis products and cannabidiol (CBD) are used by some people to fall asleep more easily. In appearance terms the chain is sleep-based: people who sleep longer and more regularly say they look fresher, carry less under-eye darkness and recover better from training, so a product that helps them fall asleep is seen as supporting those looks goals indirectly [15].

CBD is a non-intoxicating cannabis constituent, while THC is the main intoxicating one. The only FDA-approved CBD medicine, Epidiolex (2018), is indicated for certain seizure disorders, not sleep [1][11]. Wikipedia notes that CBD may help with pain, sleep and addiction according to some claims, that clinical evidence is limited, and that somnolence is a common effect [1].

Research on cannabis and sleep is mixed. A 2023 randomised crossover trial in adults with insomnia tested a THC-and-CBD medicinal cannabis oil against placebo and reported improved sleep, a 2023 systematic review of 34 studies found CBD alone or with equal THC may relieve insomnia symptoms but that only two of the studies enrolled people with insomnia, and a 2025 meta-analysis of polysomnography studies found cannabis does not consistently change sleep duration, latency or staging, with withdrawal from regular use associated with sleep disturbance [3][10][4].

chain: Cannabis or CBD taken in the evening
Easier sleep onset, as users report
More sleep supports fresher skin and training recovery
angle.text: People use cannabis or CBD products at night hoping to fall asleep faster, and better sleep is widely linked in the community with a rested face and better training recovery. The effect on sleep itself varies by product and person in the research.

infobox: Smoked or vaped cannabis, edibles, CBD oils, gummies, hemp flower[5][6][7]
Varies; US hemp-derived CBD at or under 0.3% THC unscheduled federally, but not lawful as a food or supplement[1][12]
Mixed results in trials, systematic reviews and meta-analyses[3][10][4]
Sleep disturbance and REM rebound reported on stopping regular use[4][14]

paras: Users take cannabis by smoking, vaping or edibles, and CBD as oils, gummies or hemp flower, often in the evening [5][6]. On T Nation, one poster described using a high-CBD edible alongside a calming supplement and said it worked well for sleep, while another asked what CBD oil actually does and noted that it is heavily hyped but reported better results from hemp flower [5][6].

On looksmax.org, a user weighing whether to return to cannabis after quitting nicotine wrote that he had been told weed is less harmful for looks and health than nicotine, and members compared edibles and dry-herb vaporisers [7].

Proponents link sleep to a rested-looking face, less under-eye darkness and better recovery between training sessions, which is why sleep aids are discussed in appearance communities. Wikipedia's article on periorbital dark circles lists fatigue and sleep loss among the causes that can make the skin around the eyes look paler and the blood beneath it look bluer or darker [15].

CBD was first studied in 1940 from wild hemp in Minnesota and from Egyptian Cannabis indica resin; its structure and stereochemistry were determined in 1963 by Raphael Mechoulam's group, who did the same for THC in 1964 [1][9]. Cannabis itself appears in ancient Chinese, Egyptian, Indian and Greek medical practice and entered Western medicine in the 19th century through William Brooke O'Shaughnessy [13].

The FDA approved Epidiolex, an oral CBD solution, in 2018 for seizures in Lennox-Gastaut and Dravet syndromes, and its label was expanded in 2020 to tuberous sclerosis complex [1][12]. CBD foods and beverages were widely marketed in the US from 2017; Wikipedia describes the industry as stalling during COVID-19 and collapsing by 2024 amid investor withdrawal, lack of FDA rulings and inconsistent state laws [1].

CBD side effects are dose-related and include somnolence, sedation, fatigue, diarrhea and appetite changes; Wikipedia lists insomnia and poor sleep quality among Epidiolex's side effects [1][11]. The FDA has raised concerns about liver injury, interactions with prescription drugs, gastrointestinal problems and effects on alertness and mood, and notes that male reproductive toxicity was seen in animal studies with unknown relevance to humans [11][1]. CBD may inhibit CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 enzymes and slow metabolism of some drugs [1].

Product quality studies found labeling problems: a 2017 analysis found 69% of tested US products mislabeled, and a 2020 FDA study of 147 products found about half contained THC [1]. The FDA states that CBD products are excluded from the dietary supplement definition and that adding CBD or THC to food sold across state lines is a prohibited act; in January 2023 it said existing food and supplement frameworks are not appropriate for CBD and it would work with Congress on a new pathway [12].

Legal status varies: hemp-derived CBD under 0.3% THC is unscheduled federally in the US, Canada legalised CBD in 2018 under its Cannabis Act, the EU treats it as a novel food, the UK allows products with no more than 1 mg THC and no medicinal claims, and Hong Kong prohibited it from February 2023 [1]. A 2024 review in the Annual Review of Medicine reports adverse cardiovascular, pulmonary and neuropsychiatric associations with cannabis and links intoxication to impaired driving [8].

Wikipedia's medical cannabis article reports conflicting evidence on cannabis and sleep: it says cannabis administration has no noted effect on sleep in one section, notes small improvements in chronic pain patients elsewhere, and describes withdrawal linked to less sleep, longer time to fall asleep and REM rebound; tolerance develops over days or weeks [13]. The 2025 meta-analysis likewise found withdrawal consistently associated with reduced total sleep, prolonged sleep onset and REM rebound [4].

Disturbed sleep and vivid dreams are listed among cannabis withdrawal symptoms; withdrawal symptoms occur in about half of people treated for cannabis use disorder and mostly begin in the first week of abstinence and resolve within a few weeks [14].

A 2023 double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of a medicinal cannabis oil containing THC and CBD in 29 adults with self-reported insomnia reported that 60% no longer classified as clinical insomniacs after the two-week active phase, with higher midnight melatonin and 21 more minutes of light sleep per night than placebo; the authors noted effects were more pronounced in the second phase due to a period effect and loss of blinding [3].

A 2023 systematic review in Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research of 34 eligible studies concluded CBD alone, or combined with equal THC, may help relieve insomnia symptoms, but only 2 studies enrolled people with insomnia (one a case report) and most relied on unvalidated self-report [10].

A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 polysomnography studies (nine in the meta-analysis) found no consistent change in sleep duration, latency, wake time, efficiency or stages with cannabis, noted that early REM-suppression findings came from small high-THC studies, and called for standardised protocols to resolve discrepancies between subjective sleep improvements and objective measures [4].
A phase 2 trial of cannabinoids for insomnia in major depression (n=14) was completed in 2023; its registry entry reports no results [2].

timeline.event: CBD first studied from wild hemp in Minnesota and Egyptian Cannabis indica resin. [1]
Mechoulam's group determines the structure and stereochemistry of CBD. [1][9]
The same group works out the structure of THC. [9]
DSM-5 adds cannabis withdrawal as a recognised condition. [14]
FDA approves Epidiolex for seizures in Lennox-Gastaut and Dravet syndromes; the US Farm Bill removes hemp with 0.3% THC or less from the definition of marijuana. [1][11]
FDA holds a public hearing on cannabis-derived products in May and issues warning letters to CBD marketers in November. [11][1]
Epidiolex label expanded to tuberous sclerosis complex; FDA study finds about half of 147 CBD products contained THC. [1]

A randomised crossover trial of THC/CBD oil in insomnia and a 34-study systematic review of CBD for insomnia are published; FDA says food and supplement frameworks are not appropriate for CBD. [3][10][12]
Sleep Medicine Reviews meta-analysis finds cannabis does not consistently change polysomnography sleep parameters. [4]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org and T Nation, cannabis and CBD come up as sleep aids and as part of broader questions about how substance use affects looks and health [5][6][7].

claims.claim: Cannabis or CBD helps you fall asleep.
claims.believers: T Nation posters report good results from high-CBD edibles or hemp flower for sleep, while others note that CBD is hyped [5][6].
claims.experts: A 2023 crossover trial reported improved sleep with a THC/CBD oil, a 2023 review called for larger insomnia studies, and a 2025 meta-analysis found no consistent change in polysomnography measures [3][10][4].

claims.claim: Withdrawal after regular use can worsen sleep.
claims.believers: Forum users discuss returning to cannabis after stopping and weigh it against nicotine for health and looks [7].
claims.experts: The 2025 meta-analysis found withdrawal from active use consistently associated with reduced total sleep and longer sleep onset [4].

claims.claim: CBD products are what the label says.
claims.believers: Sellers market CBD widely for sleep and calm [1].
claims.experts: A 2017 analysis found 69% of sampled products mislabeled, and a 2020 FDA study found about half of 147 contained THC [1]; the FDA says many products do not contain the CBD levels they claim [11].

claims.claim: Cannabis is less harmful for looks and health than nicotine.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster says he was told weed is less harmful for looks and health than nicotine [7].
claims.experts: A 2024 review reports adverse cardiovascular, pulmonary and neuropsychiatric associations with cannabis, and notes that perceptions of cannabis as benign contrast with emerging clinical data [8].

claims.claim: CBD is a legal, approved sleep aid.
claims.believers: CBD gummies and oils are sold widely in many places for sleep [1].
claims.experts: The FDA states Epidiolex is the only approved CBD product, for seizures, and that unapproved products have not been evaluated for efficacy, dosing or interactions [11][12].

claims.claim: CBD calms the body but can itself cause drowsiness or sleep problems.
claims.believers: A T Nation poster describes a high-CBD edible as working well for sleep [6].
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists somnolence and also insomnia and poor sleep quality as Epidiolex side effects, and the FDA lists drowsiness among common effects [1][11].
